changed.title: Majority of 7 bits (at least 4 on) has an AND/OR/NOT circuit of fan-in at most two with at most 19 gates
changed.statement: PEqualNP.MetaComplexity.HasCircuitSize 7 (fun x : Fin 7 → Bool => decide (4 ≤ (List.ofFn x).count true)) 19
changed.unlocks: a lower rung of the ladder for majority of 7, below the checked 21
changed.context: Answer with a circuit, not an argument: a gate list (operation, wires read; wires 0..6 are the input bits, gate j writes wire 7+j, each gate reads only earlier wires) and the output wire. Judged by one kernel evaluation over all 128 inputs. Any search method is welcome; only the circuit is checked. The rung at 21 is checked; we do not hold that circuit. Our own best without NOT gates is 22 (computed). We do not know whether 19 exists. If your circuit uses a NOT gate, say so.

changed.title: Exact simultaneous tree-like resolution size, depth and width for inconsistent signed graph parity constraints
changed.statement:
∀ (n : ℕ) (E : Fin n → Fin n → Bool → Prop),
  (∀ u v b, E u v b → E v u b) →
  let bad := fun m : ℕ => ∃ (v : ℕ → Fin n) (s : ℕ → Bool),
    v 0 = v m ∧ Odd (((Finset.range m).filter (fun i => s i = true)).card) ∧
    ∀ i < m, E (v i) (v (i+1)) (s i)
  let ax := fun C : PEqualNP.ProofComplexity.Clause (Fin n) =>
    ∃ (u v : Fin n) (b a : Bool), E u v b ∧ C = {(u,!a),(v,a ^^ b)}
  ∀ g : ℕ, bad g → (∀ j < g, ¬ bad j) →
    ∀ L h w : ℕ,
      (∃ (nodes inner : Finset (List Bool)) (line : List Bool → PEqualNP.ProofComplexity.Clause (Fin n)),
        [] ∈ nodes ∧ inner ⊆ nodes ∧ line [] = ∅ ∧
        (∀ p ∈ nodes, p.length ≤ h ∧ (line p).card ≤ w) ∧
        (nodes \ inner).card ≤ L ∧ (∀ p ∈ nodes, p ∉ inner → ax (line p)) ∧
        (∀ (p : List Bool) (bit : Bool), p ++ [bit] ∈ nodes → p ∈ inner) ∧
        ∀ p ∈ inner, p ++ [false] ∈ nodes ∧ p ++ [true] ∈ nodes ∧
          PEqualNP.ProofComplexity.IsResolvent (line (p ++ [false])) (line (p ++ [true])) (line p)) ↔
      2*g ≤ L ∧ 2*g ≤ 2^h ∧ (if g = 1 then 1 else 2) ≤ w
changed.unlocks: determines the exact simultaneous number of axiom leaves, height and width of a signed-graph resolution tree
changed.context: The last resolution joins opposite units. Each unit subtree must contain axioms from an inconsistent signed subgraph, since on a consistent subgraph a satisfying labelling and its complement realize both values. An inconsistent subgraph contains an odd-sign cycle on distinct edges, hence each subtree has at least g leaves. Conversely split a shortest bad cycle into balanced chains. For either initial bit, compose implications along its edges in a balanced tree to derive the opposite unit. Resolve the two units. A bad loop already gives the two unit axioms.
changed.sketch: The last resolution joins opposite units. Each unit subtree must contain axioms from an inconsistent signed subgraph, since on a consistent subgraph a satisfying labelling and its complement realize both values. An inconsistent subgraph contains an odd-sign cycle on distinct edges, hence each subtree has at least g leaves. Conversely split a shortest bad cycle into balanced chains. For either initial bit, compose implications along its edges in a balanced tree to derive the opposite unit. Resolve the two units. A bad loop already gives the two unit axioms.

changed.title: Known result rebuilt: The squared Frobenius error of the best rank-r approximation to a Hadamard matrix is n(n-r)
changed.statement:
∀ (n : ℕ) (H : Matrix (Fin n) (Fin n) ℝ), 0 < n →
  (∀ i j, H i j = 1 ∨ H i j = -1) →
  (∀ i j, (∑ c, H i c * H j c) = if i = j then (n : ℝ) else 0) →
  ∀ r : ℕ, r ≤ n →
    let err := fun (A : Matrix (Fin n) (Fin n) ℝ) => ∑ i, ∑ j, (H i j - A i j)^2
    let best : ℝ := n * (n-r : ℕ)
    (∀ A, A.rank ≤ r → best ≤ err A) ∧ (∃ A, A.rank ≤ r ∧ err A = best)
changed.unlocks: Gives the attainable squared error under a rank constraint for an orthogonal sign target.
changed.context: All singular values of H are the square root of n, so the squared norm in discarded directions is n(n-r). Alternatively project onto the column space of any approximant for the lower bound, then keep r columns of H for equality.
changed.sketch: All singular values of H are the square root of n, so the squared norm in discarded directions is n(n-r). Alternatively project onto the column space of any approximant for the lower bound, then keep r columns of H for equality.
